A region is bounded by the curve $y=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}$, the $x$-axis, and the lines $x=-1$ and $x=1$, as shown above. Find the area $A$ of the region. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-arcsin\,(\frac{x}{2}){|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =-(arcsin\,(\frac{1}{2})-arcsin\,(-\frac{1}{2})) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+(-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is 

$$
A=-{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$
